# Institutional upgrade implementation ledger

User-authorized objective, 2026-09-18: traceable important measurements, reproducible decisions, and recommendations connected to supported portfolio consequences. Preserve current working repairs, abstention, existing consumer fields and no-paid-AI policy. Production remains on AWS; GitHub Actions deploys with runner IAM.

This ledger records implementation status, not a claim that the fleet is already institutional grade. The September 18 audit and blueprint are the baseline. No model receives sizing authority simply because its code deploys.

## Acceptance workstreams

- [ ] Correct foundational performance grading, provenance and downstream trust.
- [ ] Correct shared macro transformations, source timing and market-tape meaning.
- [ ] Correct Treasury instrument comparability and residual buyback narratives.
- [ ] Extend shared observation identity, immutable capture and point-in-time contracts.

- [ ] Connect supported portfolio exposures and explicit scenarios to decision explanations.
- [ ] Extend independent-evidence ancestry and validation permissions through consumers.
- [ ] Repair shared page correctness, freshness, navigation and evidence inspection.
- [ ] Validate domain engines and migrate consumers in dependency order.
- [ ] Verify deployment receipts, live artifacts, page behavior and recovery cases.

## Stage 167: inspectable chart price/volume observations

- Production Chart QA exposed six undated historical geometric pairs labeled "confirmed" by comparing today's close with historical necklines. The old overlay silently limited the population to six, treated missing volumes as zero, included the latest bar in its unlabeled relative-volume denominator, and omitted the first complete Bollinger window. The complete 6,496-byte predecessor is retained without execution in `tests/fixtures/legacy-stock-desk-overlay.js.txt`, SHA-256 `2830168bc65574615b8a92dce44f778bfd081e6fa912f7c576c7538fc347ff97`.
- The replacement validates the complete identified chart frame and retains every input bar and geometric pair. Each pair exposes dates, observed-bar separation, neckline, dated latest-close comparison, volumes and the five subsequent observations required to identify the second extremum. Equal-price plateaus no longer manufacture repeated extrema. Pagination is presentation only; the explicit JSON download includes every row, pair, methodology limitation and both the prior-20 and legacy inclusive relative-volume definitions. Missing volumes remain unavailable; explicit zeros remain zeros. Bollinger width uses all complete 20-observation windows with empirical midrank ties and no probability or squeeze forecast claim.
- Chart acquisition binds symbol, interval and reported source to the returned bar array. Repainting old bars cannot borrow the newly selected ticker's identity. Delayed live responses cannot overwrite a different symbol, interval, generation or replay; interior/volume revisions invalidate calculations. Unchanged refreshes preserve open disclosures and page selection; malformed frames clear earlier results, and browser back/forward caching resumes exactly one timer. The existing technical renderer delegates to this panel instead of periodically restoring its old oscillator vote.
- Fourteen focused regressions cover mathematical boundaries, missing/zero/overflow data, invalid prices and clocks, complete pagination/export, source identity, delayed responses, interior revisions, DOM recovery and browser lifecycle. The final full frontend run passed 1,296 tests. Deployment checks passed 441 static and 12 candidate-shell checks. Registry drift checks pass without a registry rewrite. Preview showed 8,469 retained SPY bars, all 2,112 historical pairs and 8,450 Bollinger windows; pagination reached 26–50 without collapsing, document width stayed 1,280, and no browser console errors appeared.
- This is descriptive research on the retained chart frame. Source acquisition timing, upstream transformations/volume defaults, completion of the newest bar, corporate actions, volume units, original-provider replay and point-in-time/predictive qualification remain explicitly unverified. It grants no Calls or sizing permission. It does not rebuild or qualify the separately shipped Wyckoff campaign tools. Production manifest and live browser acceptance remain required after push.

- Production acceptance: commit `efe1accfd5b71dbaaf0c58940f8d7d8a4c31a3de`, Pages `36257870582`, page gate `36257870591`. The public build was already the concurrent descendant `e8dd6fc57da617aa5d1efcbb5518f1b2ade5339f`; git ancestry and byte comparisons confirm all four intended chart source files are unchanged there. Five live assets match that served manifest, including the complete 351,084-byte chart engine. Production SPY displays all 2,112 pairs, opens 25 dated rows, has no console errors or document overflow. Preview switching to QQQ displays its separate 6,918-bar frame ending September 10 and 1,191 pairs, without borrowing SPY dates or source identity. Durable evidence: `docs/audit/2026-09-26/chart-research-acceptance.json`.

The current Squeeze Fuel model takes the first SEC ZIP link, collapses its daily fail balances by literal symbol, discards CUSIP/price/original rows, and uses maximum balances as a forced-buying score. Its independently collected FINRA positions and FMP float overlay also need source and identity qualification. SEC CNS fails are aggregate outstanding balances on settlement dates; they are neither new daily fail flows nor proof of short-sale origin, fail age, or future forced buying. SEC's documentation also says the price is the prior day's close and a dot indicates an unavailable/sub-penny price; the file itself does not explicitly state currency or the price's observation date. Sources: https://www.sec.gov/data-research/sec-markets-data/fails-deliver-data and https://www.sec.gov/investor/pubs/regsho.htm .
